messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: cont-batch path p99 latency breached 2s in us-west-2 (service: inference-serving). Auto-pager triggered. Rollup: p95->~900ms, p99->~8s. Affected: streaming & sync generation. Link: https://grafana.redwood/inference/alerts/5001234567 :rotating_light:
alex: I'm on it, paging Maya and Jun. Any customer pages yet?
maya: no direct pages, but saw increased 504s from a couple of long-running streaming sessions. digging into traces now.
jun: looking at batcher dashboards — queue depth spiked ~00:42 UTC, avg batch size up 2.5x for some hosts. mixed-seqlen traffic looks skewed (lots of very long sequences).
ops-bot: runbook invoked: /runbook contbatch-tail-latency. Recommended mitigations: (1) enable pack-shed, (2) reduce batch_max_tokens, (3) route heavy streaming traffic to spare pool.
alex: quick mitigation: can we temporarily disable continuous batching for streaming routes? command to flip in prod feature flags?
maya: yes, we have FF key `contbatch_streaming_enabled`. I can flip to false for us-west-2. Doing it in 2m unless someone objects.
jun: +1 to flip. Also propose reducing `batch_max_tokens` from 1024 -> 384 on the affected pool to limit padding amplification. That should lower tail.
alex: go for the flag flip first. keep config change as follow-up if flag not enough.
maya: flipping `contbatch_streaming_enabled` -> false for pool usw2-batcher-1 now.
ops-bot: ACTION: feature-flag updated: contbatch_streaming_enabled=false (usw2-batcher-1).
maya: monitors show immediate drop in queue depth for streaming workers. p95 improving: 900ms -> 450ms within 30s. p99 still noisy ~2.8s.
jun: p99 hotspot traces point to KV cache thrashing on certain keys (long prompts causing large KV growth). Logs show repeated KV eviction cycles:
```
[2025-11-03T00:42:10Z] evict_kv: host=usw2-batcher-1 shard=3 evicted=1200 new_kv_items=1300
[2025-11-03T00:42:11Z] kv_miss_rate: 0.27 -> 0.62
```
jun: that explains persistent p99 even after disabling cont-batch for streaming — sync/generation still on cont-batch path.
alex: can we throttle or isolate very long seq requests? We have a scheduling fairness knob. Suggest: temporarily cap max_seq_len to 4096 for user-level routing on affected pool.
maya: we can add a routing rule to send requests with seq_len>4096 to fallback small-pool (higher cost but predictable). Will apply rule in 1m.
ops-bot: routing-change applied: route(seq_len>4096) -> fallback-dedicated-pool-usw2.
maya: after routing rule, p99 down to ~1.6s, p95 ~320ms. Good improvement.
jun: still seeing a few streaming stalls originating from older sessions that started before flag flip — those sessions are pinned to old worker ids. any way to nuke those gracefully?
alex: we can trigger a rolling drain for workers with >60s pinned streams. command: `./admin drain-workers --max-age 60 --pool usw2-batcher-1`. Be careful — draining causes brief reconnects for active streams.
maya: running drain now with `--grace 10s` to minimize impact.
ops-bot: drain initiated: 12 workers targeted. Expect transient reconnects for ~10-15 sessions.
maya: drain completed. Verified reconnect logs; around 9 streams reconnected successfully, 1 stream dropped (client retried). No customer SLA pages so far.
jun: also patched batch scheduler to enable preemptive_shed=true on the cont-batch path to evict oversized batches earlier. Patch rolled to canary 2 hosts.
alex: what's the rollout plan? we want minimal risk.
jun: canary -> monitor 10m -> gradual rollout 25% -> 50% -> 100% if metrics stable. I've set canary window.
maya: quick note on customer impact: three customers had elevated tail (internal regen monitoring) but no error spikes besides timeouts on long streaming sessions older than 30s. I alerted account team to expect follow-up.
alex: thanks. action items so far: (1) contbatch_streaming_enabled=false (done), (2) routing rule for seq_len>4096 (done), (3) drained pinned workers (done), (4) preemptive_shed canary (in progress).
jun: one more observation — model KV size for model-x86-v2 has a bug where it doesn't compact intermittently. raising bug: INF-3492. Might need model-level patch or restart.
maya: for immediate, we can schedule a staggered restart of model runtimes on affected batchers after 30m quiet window. I'll coordinate with infra.
alex: agree. Also open a post-incident task to tune `batch_max_tokens` defaults and add telemetry for mixed-seqlen amplification.
ops-bot: NOTE: PagerDuty incident created PD-84321, severity: S2.
incident-bot: Status update posted to #incidents. Customer impact: degraded latency for long-stream sessions, small number of dropped streams during drain.
maya: handing off to night oncall — Alex, I'll take over the next shift at 0400 UTC and watch rollback signals. Leaving runbook notes in the incident ticket.
alex: thanks — I'm switching to oncall monitoring for 15m then handing to Jun for final canary watch.
jun: I'll stay on until rollout finishes. If p99 rises above 3s or errors >0.2% for 5m, revert preemptive_shed and revert routing.
maya: logging final metrics snapshot into the incident ticket: pre-mitigation p95=0.9s p99=8.1s; post-mitigation p95=0.33s p99=1.5s.
alex: closing note: mitigation worked, customer impact limited. Follow-ups: INF-3492 (model KV compaction), INF-3493 (batch_max_tokens tuning), INF-3494 (add mixed-seqlen telemetry/dashboard). I'll update the incident timeline and mark for postmortem if SEV escalates. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: Incident status: mitigated -> monitoring.
incident-bot: Thread closed at 5001234887.
